stem.text: The structure of a naturally occurring compound, Q, is shown.

stem.alt: Skeletal formula of compound Q, labelled compound Q: a steroid skeleton with a ketone C=O on the left ring and a C=C in that ring, an HO group on the ring carbon next to the angular methyl, a CHO aldehyde group on the central ring, and a C(=O)CH2OH side chain on the five-membered ring.

stem.text: Compound Q is heated under reflux with an excess of acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$.

A.text: orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH and no reaction with alkaline $\text{I}_2\text{(aq)}$; yellow precipitate with alkaline $\text{I}_2\text{(aq)}$ and no reaction with Fehling’s reagent

C.text: yellow precipitate with alkaline $\text{I}_2\text{(aq)}$ and orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH; no reaction with alkaline $\text{I}_2\text{(aq)}$ and no reaction with Fehling’s reagent

D.text: yellow precipitate with alkaline $\text{I}_2\text{(aq)}$ and red precipitate with Fehling’s reagent; yellow precipitate with alkaline $\text{I}_2\text{(aq)}$ and orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH
